description: A single-panel line plot with error bars showing how substructural length scales in the 8Al steel evolve with deformation. The x-axis is "Engineering strain" (dimensionless, ticked 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30); the y-axis is "SB spacing, DC size, and DCB size (nm)", ticked 0-1400 in 200 nm steps. The legend lists exactly three series: α_SB (grey/black), γ_SB+DCB (red), γ_DC (blue) — i.e. ferrite slip-band spacing, austenite slip-band spacing plus dislocation cell block size, and austenite dislocation cell size. Points are plotted at four engineering strains: one just above 0.00, and three at/close to the 0.10, 0.20 and 0.25-0.30 ticks. All three quantities decrease monotonically with strain: the red γ_SB+DCB curve is highest at every strain, starting just below the 1000 nm gridline and ending between the 200 and 400 nm gridlines; the grey α_SB curve starts just below the 800 nm gridline and falls to just above the 100 nm gridline; the blue γ_DC curve is defined only at the two highest strains, lying between the red and grey curves (near 300 nm at the higher-mid strain and near 150 nm at the highest). Error bars are present on all points and are widest at the lowest strain (the red bar runs from about the 500 nm gridline up to between the 1200 and 1400 nm gridlines). The figure demonstrates continuous refinement of slip bands in both austenite and ferrite and of austenite dislocation cell blocks/cells with increasing strain, supplying the D values used in the flow-stress equations. The plot has a light blue gradient background (apparent rendering artefact) and no gridlines are drawn.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line plot with three series versus engineering strain; the y-axis is labelled 'SB spacing, DC size, and DCB size (nm)' with ticks 0 to 1400 in 200 nm increments and the x-axis 'Engineering strain' with ticks 0.00 to 0.30 in 0.05 increments.
The legend gives exactly three entries as printed: α_SB (grey/black curve), γ_SB+DCB (red curve) and γ_DC (blue curve).
All three series decrease monotonically with increasing engineering strain; the red γ_SB+DCB curve is the highest at every measured strain and the grey α_SB curve is the lowest.
The blue γ_DC series is plotted only at the two highest strains (near 0.20 and near 0.28), where it lies between the red γ_SB+DCB and grey α_SB curves.
Vertical error bars are drawn on every data point and are widest at the lowest strain; the red error bar there extends from about the 500 nm gridline up to between the 1200 and 1400 nm gridlines.
Data points are plotted at only four engineering-strain values, the lowest just above 0.00 and the highest between the 0.25 and 0.30 ticks; no numeric data labels are printed at the points.

The caption states the figure reports the average slip band (SB) spacing, dislocation cell block (DCB) size and dislocation cell (DC) size in austenite of the 8Al steel, plus the average slip band spacing in ferrite of the 8Al steel, at different deformation stages.

The citing text states that the deformation stages are 3 %, 10 %, 20 % and 28 % engineering strain, and that these correspond to the substructure development (slip bands, then dislocation cell blocks and cells in austenite, plus deformation twins at 28 %) illustrated in Fig. 5.
The citing text states that the mean slip band spacing D from Fig. 6 is used in a Taylor-type flow-stress equation with K a geometrical factor, M = 2.8, G = 80.7 GPa and b = 0.25 nm.

The citing text states that in a second similitude-based equation M_SB = M_DCB = 3.06 and M = 2.44, G = 70 GPa, b = 0.25 nm, D is the slip band spacing, dislocation cell block size or dislocation cell size, and 0.8 and 0.2 are the area fractions of dislocation cell blocks and dislocation cells respectively.

The citing text states that calculated and measured flow stress σ_tot for 8Al steel are given in Table 4 and Fig. 9(b), with the calculations using Eqs. (5)-(8) and the data of Fig. 6 — establishing this figure as the source of the length-scale input to the flow-stress model.

subfigures.description: Line plot of three error-bar series versus engineering strain (0.00-0.30): α_SB (grey), γ_SB+DCB (red) and γ_DC (blue) against y-axis 'SB spacing, DC size, and DCB size (nm)' from 0 to 1400. All series decrease monotonically; γ_SB+DCB is uppermost, γ_DC exists only at the two highest strains.

unreadable_items: Exact engineering-strain abscissa values of the four data points are not printed as labels and must be estimated between the x-axis ticks (lowest point lies between 0.00 and 0.05; highest between 0.25 and 0.30).
Curve-derived y-values are read relative to the 200 nm gridlines; no numeric values are printed at the data points.
